newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up on pre-weekend short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up on pre-weekend short covering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Friday in a lethargic session, with shortcovering ahead of the weekend driving the complex into positive territory, industry sources said.
June climbed 5.4 cents to close at $2.249 per million British thermal units. July settled 6.5 cents higher at $2.265. Other deferreds ended up by one to 6.1 cents.

"It was a lot of short covering, but there could have been some fund buying too - the whole strip was up," said one East Coast trader, adding June was well-offered at $2.28 and a break above that number could trigger more buying.

Traders said there were mixed views about next week's forecasts, which are calling for seasonal to slightly below-seasonal weather in the Northeast, Midwest and West, with Texas and the South expected to warm to above-normal.

Technical traders said the market was range-bound, with June support in the $2.15 area and resistance at $2.30. A break of $2.15 should lead to a test of major support at $2.05. Further resistance was seen at the $2.43 contract high.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend prices slipped a nickel Friday to the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes were off more than five cents to the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also lost some ground to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip gained 4.3 cents to $2.277. NYMEX said 34,969 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 41,246.

On KCBT, June finished 1.3 cents higher at $2.071, while deferreds ended up by two to three cents. The East/West spread widened by 4.1 cents to 17.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 61 contracts traded, down sharply from Thursday's total of 445.
